responses.response: Three red water buckets are in view around the well.

evidence.fact: Looking down at the circular well, three red buckets are clearly visible at the stone rim (left, center, right); people partly block the far side.

details.counting_basis: Only red buckets clearly visible above the well rim at 01:57 are counted; any bucket fully hidden behind people on the far side is excluded.
details.deduplication_rule: Each bucket is identified by its position/rope and counted once while visible; none has left and re-entered the frame yet.

responses.response: A fourth red bucket has come into view at the near edge, so four are visible now.
responses.trigger_type_reason: The change is a bucket entering the frame as the camera tilts; only vision reveals it.

evidence.fact: The camera angle lowers and a fourth red bucket resting at the near rim enters the frame, alongside the left, center and right rim buckets.

details.counting_basis: Four red buckets are visible at 02:03 after the near-rim bucket re-enters the frame due to the camera tilt.
details.deduplication_rule: The newly revealed near-rim bucket is a distinct physical bucket, not a re-appearance of one already in the set; the three rim buckets keep their identities, so no double counting.

responses.response: The camera has moved on to the paved area; no red buckets are in view now.
responses.trigger_type_reason: The count drops to zero because the well leaves the frame; this is purely visual.

evidence.fact: The frame now shows the white-painted hopscotch court on stone slabs; the well and its red buckets are out of view.

details.counting_basis: No red buckets are present in the frame from 02:04 onward as the camera has left the well.
details.deduplication_rule: The current set is empty; the well buckets are out of frame and are not counted, and they do not reappear later in the video.

question: Whenever both friends in the video are visibly in the frame together—either directly or as their full shadows—let me know; isolated hands or feet don't count.

responses.response: Both friends are in frame together right now—the woman in the black cap and grey mask and the woman in the pink cap.
responses.trigger_type_reason: The count of friends present is read purely from who is visible in the frame; no audio cue is needed.

trigger.definition: Both friends are visibly present in the frame together, either directly or as full shadows; isolated hands or feet do not count.

details.counting_basis: Both friends are directly visible together in the selfie; each is one distinct person, counted once.
details.deduplication_rule: Count only distinct individuals presently in frame; partial limbs in other shots are ignored, so the figure-count resets to 0 between shots.

responses.response: Both friends are together again—their two full-body shadows are side by side on the cobblestones.
responses.trigger_type_reason: Reappearance is confirmed by two distinct full-body shadow silhouettes in the frame; audio adds nothing to the count.

evidence.fact: The vlog's two subjects are the two friends introduced in the opening selfie.
A downward shot of cobblestones shows two full human shadows side by side, one raising an arm in a peace sign, indicating both walkers are in frame.

trigger.definition: Both friends are visibly present in the frame together, either directly or as full shadows; isolated hands or feet do not count.

details.counting_basis: Two distinct full-body shadow silhouettes lie on the cobblestones; as the vlog's two walkers introduced at the start, these map to the same two friends, so the current count is 2.
details.deduplication_rule: The shadows are mapped to the two friends already introduced rather than treated as new objects; hands-only or feet-only appearances elsewhere are not counted, preventing double counting.
